name: DHCP
soc_note: A new host on the lab network should get the address you planned

name: DNS
soc_note: Odd DNS from a lab VM is worth a second look. Do not query domains you do not have a reason to touch

name: HTTP
soc_note: Port 80 on a management page is a reason to ask why TLS is missing

name: HTTPS
soc_note: The Wazuh dashboard is often reached over HTTPS. Confirm the port in your install guide

name: SSH
soc_note: Week 3 checks that root SSH login is off

name: RDP
soc_note: Keep RDP on the host-only lab network. Do not publish 3389 to the internet

name: SMB
soc_note: Unexpected SMB toward the internet is a classic alert. This sheet does not ask you to probe SMB

name: LDAP
soc_note: You will meet it again beside identity in Week 8

name: LDAPS
soc_note: Prefer the TLS version when a directory crosses a network

name: Kerberos
soc_note: Failed Kerberos shows up in Windows security logs

name: SMTP
soc_note: Useful context for phishing mail you analyse defensively in Week 10

name: NTP
soc_note: Log times are hard to trust if clocks drift

name: Syslog
soc_note: One way hosts send logs. Your lab may use an agent instead

name: Wazuh-agent
purpose: Agent enrolment and events to the manager
soc_note: Plan these on 192.168.56.10. Confirm ports in the Wazuh version you install

name: MySQL
soc_note: Week 6 is about who can reach a database and how queries are built

name: PostgreSQL
soc_note: Same question as MySQL: do not expose it beyond the lab

name: WinRM
soc_note: 5986 is the HTTPS variant. Treat it as admin access

name: IP (no port)
soc_note: A wrong mask or gateway breaks the path before a port matters

name: TCP (no single port)
soc_note: Logs may show a completed handshake or only a failed attempt

name: UDP (no single port)
soc_note: DNS and DHCP use it. Loss looks different from a TCP reset
